# Hyperchunk subset in CUDA Craft

Repository: https://github.com/Soju06/hyperchunk
Revision: `387c9ad30ac1b4eddbcaad31a02e8864d5b394c1`
License: MIT, retained in `LICENSE` (Copyright 2026 Soju06).

CUDA Craft statically links the C11 RNG, noise/density, aquifer, ore-vein,
surface, biome-zoom/temperature, and cave/canyon modules. The upstream target is
Minecraft 26.2. CUDA Craft supplies **1.21.11** configuration data and compares
its own output with 1.21.11 reference captures. Upstream parity claims do not
transfer to this adaptation.

Local changes (four files, exact patches and resulting hashes recorded):

- `biome_zoom.c`: portable `HUGE_VAL`/`NAN` constants and `<math.h>` for MSVC C11.
- `hc_df.h`, `df_compile.c`, `df_eval.c`: the pre-26.2
  `weird_scaled_sampler`, both rarity mappings, input dependency propagation and
  classification as dependent on Y. SIMD dispatch remains scalar on this MSVC build.

Floating-point contraction is not enabled; the MSVC build uses `/fp:precise`.
The integration uses bounded arenas and per-world caches on the server thread.
`tools/hyperchunk-manifest.json` pins every original and adapted file.
`tools/fetch-hyperchunk.ps1` reproduces and verifies both sets of hashes.
The byte patch file is generated by `tools/prepare-hyperchunk-patches.py`.

Structures, feature placement, fluid postprocessing, the region scheduler and
the upstream server/export tools are not linked. Optional Java reference runs
are test tooling only; the native server never starts a Java process.
